headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: Gemini CLI can ingest shared files/MCP outputs while Perplexity returns web-derived content that may be treated as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git. Perplexity can produce web-derived browsing context and uploaded-document outputs. That creates a default pathway where content from Perplexity can be copied into Gemini CLI and parsed as instructions, with no provenance barrier documented.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is copied into a file or MCP-fed prompt consumed by Gemini CLI
IF Gemini CLI treats file content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable file-based prompt ingestion for the pair
Use a separate workspace directory for Gemini CLI
Require explicit provenance tags before Gemini CLI follows external text
Review any MCP server configuration before enabling it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs/search providers. If the same workspace contains sensitive files, Gemini can expose them into prompts or outputs that are then uploaded to Perplexity, creating a default leakage path in shared-workspace use. The reverse path is less direct, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the Gemini CLI workspace
IF those files or excerpts are pasted/uploaded into Perplexity
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use Perplexity only with redacted excerpts
Run Gemini CLI in a separate sandboxed directory
Turn off automatic document upload to Perplexity
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; Perplexity cannot write locally, but it can still influence shared work products through uploaded documents and browsing context. The main conflict is on shared mutable artifacts when Gemini acts on Perplexity-derived content, not direct simultaneous writes. Because Gemini has broad write power and the pair shares filesystem-based state, conflict is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or cwd
IF Gemini CLI commits or rewrites files based on Perplexity-derived content
mitigations: Use separate branches for each agent
Lock the repo before Gemini writes
Have Perplexity work on read-only copies
Review diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces search-backed answers and citations, and Gemini CLI can act on tool outputs in the terminal. If Gemini consumes Perplexity output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes, shell actions, or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer higher severity is high.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses Perplexity answers as factual ground truth
IF Gemini CLI then edits files, runs commands, or commits based on those answers
mitigations: Require a human verification step before acting on Perplexity outputs
Cross-check critical facts against primary sources
Limit Gemini CLI to draft-only mode for Perplexity-sourced tasks
Annotate which claims came from search versus local files
requires-engineering: add citation validation before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and sends queries/documents to vendor APIs/search providers, while Gemini CLI can handle local files and shell environment. If regulated data from Gemini's workspace is uploaded into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a moderate compliance mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-sensitive data is present in Gemini CLI files
IF that data is uploaded or pasted into Perplexity
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity
Use a data-classification checklist before sharing content
Strip identifiers from prompts and documents
Keep compliance-sensitive work in Gemini-only local workflows
requires-engineering: formalize a DPA/residency review
